# Dependency redistribution record

Date: 2026-10-20. This records step 1 requirements for the current development build. It does **not** clear an installer for distribution. No installer or public download has been produced.

`inventory.json` contains 270 Rust normal/build dependencies for Windows x64 and 326 package records from the installed Qt 6.8.3 SBOMs. Build tools and unused installed Qt modules are included in those counts; they are not all shipped runtime dependencies. `licenses/` retains upstream notices found locally; `qt-sbom/` retains the original package evidence. Generate the Cargo input with the command below, then run `scripts/collect_dependency_notices.py`. A missing top-level license file does not mean that a crate has no license: workspace crates inherit the retained LiveKit root license, while some external crates put their notices in source headers or upstream repositories. Complete those sources/notices during packaging.

| Component | Observed terms and required packaging work |
| --- | --- |
| LiveKit C++ 1.12.3 / Rust a6f93a16 | Root Apache-2.0 texts retained. Preserve copyright/license and any upstream NOTICE, identify modified files and our patches, and retain exact source archives/build instructions. Our wrapper omits the internal UniFFI C++ build-version adapter; the Rust FFI still includes UniFFI. See [Apache section 4](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). |
| C++ static dependencies | Protobuf BSD-style, Abseil Apache-2.0, spdlog MIT with bundled fmt notices, nlohmann/json MIT. Retain their notices and nested third-party attribution. Versions and archive hashes are pinned in the CMake patch and dependency lock. |
| Qt 6.8.3 | Use the installed module SBOMs to select the licensing route for each **shipped** library/plugin. Current QtLibraryInfo declares a commercial/LGPL-3.0/GPL alternative. For an LGPL route, include applicable texts/notices and corresponding Qt source access, preserve permitted replacement/relinking and reverse engineering for debugging modifications. Test that a compatible replacement DLL works. Do not ship GPL-only private test helpers simply because they are installed. Qt build tools have their own licenses/exceptions. See [Qt's LGPL text](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/lgpl.html); that live page currently describes a newer Qt, so local 6.8.3 SBOMs remain the package evidence. |
| WebRTC webrtc-89d790b | Retain the **entire** aggregate `licenses/webrtc/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`; the top WebRTC BSD notice alone is insufficient. Preserve the exact prebuilt archive hash, GN arguments, source revision, and third-party source/build provenance before shipping. |
| FFmpeg inside WebRTC | GN has `ffmpeg_branding="Chrome"`, H.264 enabled, and `is_component_build=false`. The matching packaged Chrome/win/x64 config says LGPL 2.1 or later and CONFIG_GPL=0 / CONFIG_NONFREE=0. The aggregate license includes several FFmpeg license texts, including GPL; its presence alone does not prove GPL code was enabled. Retain matching complete source, actual build configuration, modifications and a compliant relinking/replacement route for the statically included components. Our outer LiveKit DLL does not itself prove those obligations are satisfied. [FFmpeg's checklist](https://www.ffmpeg.org/legal.html) explains its source/configuration requirements. |
| OpenH264 / H.264 | The aggregate includes Cisco's source BSD notice. This WebRTC artifact contains OpenH264; selecting NVIDIA for our encoder does not remove it from the SDK. Do not assume Cisco's separate precompiled binary patent-licensing arrangement covers a statically rebuilt library or this package. Establish the exact distribution route and applicable codec/patent terms before release. |
| libyuv | Exact git submodule revision and archive hash retained in the lock/build script. Preserve upstream LICENSE/PATENTS and matching source; the WebRTC aggregate also carries libyuv attribution. The application build now statically compiles this pinned revision itself (`scripts/prepare-libyuv.ps1` verifies the archive hash before extraction) for captured-content conversion, so these notices also cover libyuv objects inside `GoodSharing.exe`. |
| soxr-sys native C | The Rust wrapper manifest inherits Apache-2.0, but its compiled `src/soxr.c` explicitly says LGPL v2.1. The inventory's Rust license field does not override native code licenses. Source-header notices are retained separately, including Ooura FFT attribution. Package the matching source, LGPL text, notices and a compliant relinking route; resolve the upstream LICENCE referenced by these headers. |
| Rust dependencies | Most declare MIT/Apache/BSD/ISC/Unicode alternatives. UniFFI 0.31.2 components declare MPL-2.0: retain notices and provide covered source and any modifications under the applicable terms. Keep exact Cargo.lock and selected license choices; distinguish runtime code from build/proc-macro tools. See [MPL sections 3.1–3.4](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/). |
| Windows / MSVC / GPU | Use supported Windows system components and the appropriate Microsoft redistributable runtime. Do not copy SDK files or GPU-driver DLLs into the installer. Determine actual runtime imports and package only permitted redistributables. Project-local Rust, protoc and libclang are build dependencies. |

Regeneration, from the same signed-in account used for the project-local Rust build:

```powershell
$env:RUSTUP_HOME="$PWD\.tools\rustup"
$env:CARGO_HOME="$PWD\.tools\cargo"
$env:RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN='1.97.1'
.tools/cargo/bin/cargo.exe tree --manifest-path .deps/sources/rust-a6f93a16/rust-sdks-a6f93a16/Cargo.toml --locked --offline --package livekit-ffi --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --edges normal,build --prefix none --format '{p}|{l}' > artifacts/rust-licenses-tree.txt
python scripts/collect_dependency_notices.py
```

Release work remains: enumerate the final deployed DLLs/QML plugins and transitive native components, complete missing notices/license texts, preserve corresponding source and source offers/links, choose and verify required replacement/relinking procedures, resolve codec terms, and include an accessible third-party notice view in the packaged application. Local functionality tests do not complete this release work.

The cryptor parser repair recompiles one upstream Apache-2.0 translation unit from WebRTC revision `89d790b`, SHA-256 `a0ad0713525437fd53dd23127e10a093442a4e7f827f22bd0b54907626c582da`. Its copyright/license header is retained in the generated source and cumulative SDK patch. `scripts/prepare_frame_cryptor.py` and `patches/webrtc-89d790b-frame-crypto.patch` record the modifications; the dependency lock records the original source URL/hash. A dedicated archive copy excludes the original cryptor object and the two receiver objects described below, while preserving the pristine prebuilt library and aggregate licenses. Include this modified source/patch and its provenance in the final source/notice inventory; the release work above remains open.

The startup pipeline change additionally modifies the pinned Rust SDK's `webrtc-sys` peer-connection callback, frame-cryptor and packet-trailer headers/C++/CXX bindings, their `libwebrtc/src/native` Rust wrappers, and `livekit/src/room/e2ee/manager.rs`. It adds an early closed receiver, deferred metadata attachment and explicit activation after observer setup. Original Apache-2.0 headers are retained. `scripts/prepare_livekit_engine.py` and `patches/closed_frame_transformer.h` reproduce these edits in the cumulative `patches/livekit-rust-a6f93a16-shutdown.patch`; retain them with the final modified-source inventory.

The receiver clock bridge recompiles the exact `audio/channel_receive.cc` and `video/rtp_video_stream_receiver2.cc` units from WebRTC revision `89d790b`, retaining their BSD copyright/license headers. `scripts/prepare_receiver_clock.py`, `patches/webrtc-89d790b-receiver-clock.patch` and the dependency lock record original URLs, SHA-256 hashes and matching header checksums. The build explicitly removes each corresponding original object from its private archive copy and compiles one patched replacement; it does not suppress duplicate symbols. Retain both original source units, generated modifications, `patches/receiver_media_clock.h` and the cumulative SDK/FFI changes in the final modified-source inventory.

The separate local clock experiment builds LiveKit server v1.13.10 with the existing Go 1.26.1 toolchain, project-local module/build caches and read-only `go.mod`/`go.sum`. Its opt-in report-interval patch retains the upstream default and Apache-2.0 headers. The exact source archive, module sums, patch, recipes and binary provenance are recorded in `dependencies.lock.json` and the experiment's `build-info.json`; the official release server remains separate. The server's root license is retained under `licenses/livekit-server/`. This experiment adds statically linked Go dependencies whose notices/source obligations are not yet collected into the existing Rust/Qt inventory. It is a local test artifact, not a redistributable server release; complete the Go dependency notice inventory and applicable source obligations before distributing it.
